newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq proposes standards hike for listings.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq proposes standards hike for listings.

text.p: Nasdaq Stock Market said Wednesday it was considering raising the financial standards for companies traded on both its National Market and SmallCap Market, a move that could affect 400 small cap companies.

Nasdaq (National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations system) said it will seek public comment until December 20 before the market's board of directors meets January 27. The proposed changes would have to be approved by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Among the changes proposed are requirements governing the make-up of boards of directors and companies' worth.
"Our goal is to strike the proper balance between access to capital for companies and investment quality for investors," said Nasdaq President Alfred Berkeley in a release.

"The changes proposed for corporate governance, particularly the requirement of shareholder approval for the corporate issuance of new stock, should prevent some of the problems associated with small public companies."
The changes propose increasing listing standards at least 50 percent on both the Nasdaq SmallCap Market and the Nasdaq National Market.
Under the proposals, stocks trading at less than $1 would no longer be permitted on the Nasdaq National or SmallCap markets.
Also being proposed is making SmallCap Market companies subject to the same corporate governance standards for those on the National Market.
This includes requiring a minimum of two independent directors; an audit committee with a majority of independent directors; and shareholder approval for large, below-market issuances.
To enter the SmallCap Market, companies would need $4 million minimum in net tangible assets and at least one million shares outstanding with a minimum market value of $5 million.
Presently, there is no net minimum tangible asset requirement and companies need only 100,000 shares outstanding with a minimum market value of $1 million for SmallCap Market entry.
To remain listed, companies would need at least $2 million in net tangible assets.
Companies potentially affected represent about 29.9 percent of SmallCap listed companies and $3.9 billion of total SmallCap Market capitalization, Nasdaq said.
Proposed changes would affect 176 companies on the National Market. Nasdaq said this represents 4.5 percent of the companies listed and $4.2 billion of National Market capitalization.
Entry requirements for the National Market would be raised to minimums of $6 million in net tangible assets, $1 million in pre-tax income and $8 million in market value.
Current minumums are $4 million in net tangible assets, $750,000 in pre-tax income and $3 million in public float market value.
To remain listed, companies would have to establish at least $4 million in net tangible assets.
